Hi Aisha/Tom —

Thanks again for the call today — great overview of the Acme Logistics use case. As promised, below is a concise recap of the integration and dedicated-capacity architecture items we discussed, plus concrete next steps so we can size a Dedicated pool and plan the technical deep-dive.

Quick summary of Acme ask:
- Real-time parsing + structured output from driver status updates (low variability, 100–200 tokens per request).
- Reranking/embeddings for routing and lookup (batched nightly re-index).
- SLO: 95th pct request latency < 400ms for inference; throughput target ~80 QPS baseline with 250 QPS peak bursts.
- Data residency: US-only, private deployment preferred (Dedicated with VPC).

What we need from you (small ask to finalize sizing):
1) Typical QPS (baseline) and peak QPS for the week of a large rollout (you mentioned 80 baseline / 250 peak — confirm).
2) Avg tokens per request (you said ~150 average, confirm min/max).
3) Expected concurrency per API key/service (how many simultaneous calls from the routing layer?).
4) Any strict cold-start limits or latency SLOs tighter than 400ms.
5) Whether you’ll use SSO (SAML/Okta) for control plane access and if keys must be rotated monthly.

What we propose (high level):
- Dedicated pool (GPU-backed) with autoscaling governed by target QPS and queue depth.
- Per-route concurrency caps + request queues to smooth spikes and preserve tail latency.
- Use our SDK + token-based auth for service-to-service calls; optional mTLS for VPC.
- Structured output via tool-calling/JSON schemas; embeddings pipeline for nightly re-ranks.

Attachments: dedicated-sizing-proposal.pdf (initial sizing & cost ranges), redwood-mou-template.pdf (procurement doc).

Next steps / proposed timeline:
- You send the numbers above by EOD Tue 21 Apr -> we’ll produce a sizing proposal.
- Technical deep-dive with Dev (integration + auth) and Vivek (runtime sizing) — 60 minutes — propose Wed 22 Apr 10:00 PT.
- Optional contract/PO track with Laura in procurement after sizing.

I'll follow up with proposed agenda for the technical call.

Thanks Marissa — solid recap. A few quick answers and clarifications from our side:

- Baseline QPS: 75–90 (we see 80 on average). Peak burst: 220–280 for major route changes.
- Avg tokens per request: 140 typical; 40–600 range depending on extended driver notes.
- Concurrency: our routing tier allows up to 200 concurrent requests for the service token; we can restrict at the gateway if needed.
- Latency SLO: aiming for 95th < 350ms if possible.
- Auth: we will use Okta SAML for console access; service-to-service will be short-lived bearer tokens. Monthly key rotation is preferred.

Two questions:
1) How does Redwood autoscale Dedicated pools during an incoming burst? Is there queueing that can absorb short spikes without spinning up GPUs?
2) For embeddings/rerank jobs, can those be scheduled to a separate queue/pool to avoid interfering with low-latency inference?

Hi Tom/Aisha —

Quick answers to the two points and a few integration notes so your infra team can look ahead:

Autoscaling + queueing behavior:
- Dedicated pools autoscale based on measured throughput and queue depth. Short spikes (sub-30s) are buffered by in-ingress request queues (configurable up to N requests / route) and by our KV/prefix caches which often eliminate repeated compute for similar prompts.
- If sustained traffic exceeds buffer thresholds, we scale GPUs on a policy (min replicas, scale step, cooldown). Cooldown default is 60s to avoid oscillation.
- You can set a hard concurrency cap per route/service token; requests beyond that are queued with an in-flight timeout (fail-fast or queue-and-wait behavior is configurable).

Embeddings/rerank separation:
- Yes — embeddings and batch rerank jobs can be placed on a separate node pool (lower-cost GPUs, scheduled off-peak) and prioritized lower than low-latency inference. We recommend a dedicated batch pool for nightly re-index jobs.

SDK & auth notes for integration:
- SDK supports both API key bearer tokens and mTLS. For service-to-service we recommend short-lived bearer tokens minted by your token service and configured in our SDK.
- For structured output/tool calling, the SDK has helper primitives that validate model output against a JSON schema and support tool hooks (we can share examples in the deep-dive).
- Routing: route by policy (latency-first vs cost-first). You can pin critical routes to a smaller set of high-SLO GPUs and let best-effort routes use lower-cost variants.

I'll attach a short sample SDK config in the technical call notes, but high-level example:
- auth: token endpoint -> SDK obtains token -> uses Bearer for requests
- client config: route_priority: [low_latency, cost_optimized] ; concurrency_limit: 60 ; queue_policy: immediate-fail/queue-30s

Happy to walk through live code on Wed.

Cheers,

Tom/Aisha — adding the sizing perspective so the technical call can be concrete.

Inputs (based on your numbers + typical token latencies):
- Baseline QPS: 80, Avg tokens/request: 140 -> ~11,200 tokens/sec baseline.
- Peak burst: 250 QPS -> ~35,000 tokens/sec peak.
- Target tail latency: 95th < 350ms.

Recommendation (initial Dedicated pool):
- Start with a pool sized to handle ~1.5x baseline sustained load: plan for ~17,000 tokens/sec capacity. That gives headroom and allows autoscale to handle peaks without immediate spin-up.
- GPUs: 4x A100 80GB (or equivalent) as a starting config for the production pool; add a separate 2x cheaper-GPU batch pool for embeddings.
- Concurrency caps per model instance: 16 concurrent streams (configurable) to keep per-token latency stable. With 4 GPUs and N model instances per GPU, you get predictable concurrency headroom.
- Queueing: allow route-level queue depth of ~150 requests with configurable timeout; configure immediate-fail for critical SLA endpoints to avoid head-of-line blocking.

Autoscale behavior:
- Short burst absorption: in-ingress queue + caching will handle spikes under ~30s.
- Sustained > cooldown -> add additional replicas in steps (add 1–2 GPUs per scale event) with a 60s cooldown.
- We recommend scale-to-zero disabled for Dedicated pools to avoid cold-starts.

Cost/ops note: 1.5x baseline reduces churn and keeps request latencies stable while autoscale handles growth. We'll surface a cost tradeoff in the sizing PDF.

I'll walk through concrete numbers on Wed with the workloads you share.

— Vivek
